input.title: Verify in production: the verify-in-production discipline reaches members
input.body:
#1092 landed the verify-in-production skill (basics v13), the merge-to-main step that invokes it (git-github v7), and the engine's `Not-before:` adoption carry. None of it could be watched working in the landing session: the packs prove out only when a member's converge delivers them, and the carry only when a real tick adopts a dated request — this issue is itself that request.

Original-issue: #1091
In-production-when: `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `.claudinite-checks.json` stamps `packVersions.basics` at 13 or higher and `packVersions.git-github` at 7 or higher.
Verify: Shepherd's mount file `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md` exists and contains `Retry-every:`, and its `.claudinite/shared/packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md` names verify-in-production as a post-merge step. Additionally, this issue's own work item was born `task:blocked` rather than picked before its `Not-before:` — that is the adoption carry observed live.
Blocked-by: #1092
Not-before: 2026-08-21T08:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

Instructions to the run — execute this playbook, decide nothing:

1. Read `In-production-when:` against Shepherd's raw `.claudinite-checks.json` on its default branch. Never infer it from a merge, a green run, or elapsed time.
2. Live → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the stamped versions, the file contents found) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1091 with a comment saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed.
3. Not yet live → push `Not-before:` forward by 1 day, re-apply `claude-task` and `claude-model:sonnet`, and leave this issue open. No comment.

content.text:
Merged and productionized end to end:

- [PR #1092](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1092) squash-merged as `8da4c91`, closing [#1091](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1091). Local `main` synced, conversation captured (351 entries).
- The merge recipe's new step 7 then ran for the first time — on this very change, which is exactly the case it exists for: filed [#1095](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1095), marked `claude-task` + `claude-model:sonnet`, `Not-before: 2026-08-21T08:00:00Z`, `Retry-every: 1 day`. It waits for Shepherd's stamp to carry `basics ≥ 13` and `git-github ≥ 7`, then verifies the mounted skill files — and its own adoption as `task:blocked` doubles as the live proof of the engine's `Not-before:` carry. On failure it reopens #1091.

> ✅ All done — the queue takes it from here; #1095 verifies itself once Shepherd converges.

{"id":5202175025,"number":1091,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"A change that can only be proven in production files its own verification, automatically","body":"Today the loop that proves a change actually works stops at the merge. Anything whose effect only appears somewhere else — a vendored pack reaching a member, a deployed site, a prose rule that only exists in the *next* session — is verified when the owner happens to ask for it, or not at all. Yesterday's checkbox rule is the example: it landed green, and it took the owner asking to find out whether it closed a real issue on a real repo.

`basics/RULES.md` already says the right thing twice — *watch it work now*, and *when verifying now is genuinely impossible, make the follow-up a mechanism that comes to you*. What is missing is the mechanism, and the discipline of reaching for it without being asked.

**Land two things in `basics`:**

- A **skill** that fires at the end of a change, beside the conversation capture, and decides whether the change is one whose proof lives in production. When it is, it files a verification issue naming the production condition and the assertion. The discernment is the substance: a change already proven by a test that ran, a comment, a design doc, a UI feature with an executable-requirements test, anything watched working this session — none of those file anything.
- A **task** that picks those issues up, re-derives whether the change is live yet, and either runs the assertion or leaves the issue for the next run. Not live yet is silence, not a comment; a condition that never comes true gives up at a stated date rather than waiting forever.

"In production" is per-project and belongs in the issue rather than in config: a pack change is live when a member's stamp carries a version past the change's, a site change when the live version # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
